# Frequently Asked Questions

## Cost and Terms

### What does it cost?

$22,000 per project for the full academic year. This matches the BYU engineering capstone
sponsorship fee.

### What does the fee cover?

Faculty oversight and direction, student team time across two semesters, software and API costs,
data and tooling access, program administration, and the final delivery showcase.

### When is payment due?

Payment terms and vendor setup are handled through BYU. Contact the program director and we will
connect you with the right administrative contact early, so vendor onboarding does not delay the
project start.

### Is there a formal agreement?

Yes. Sponsorship is confirmed in writing before the project starts, covering scope, fee, IP,
and confidentiality.

## Intellectual Property and Confidentiality

### Who owns the work?

You do. Sponsors retain all deliverables and intellectual property, including code, models,
documents, and analysis.

### Will students sign an NDA?

Yes. Every student on the team signs your NDA, or the Foundry's standard mutual NDA if you
prefer. This happens before any data is shared.

### How is our data handled?

Client data stays in the approved project repository and approved tools. It does not go into
students' personal accounts, personal cloud storage, or unapproved AI services. Students delete
local copies at the end of the engagement. Data handling terms can be tightened to match your
requirements.

### Can students talk about the project publicly?

Not without your written permission. That includes LinkedIn, portfolios, and job interviews.
The default is that the engagement is confidential. Many sponsors do grant permission for a
general description, which helps students and costs you nothing, but it is your call.

### Do you use AI tools on our data?

Yes, that is the point of the program, and it is governed. Students use approved tools only,
under your data handling terms. If you have a specific list of permitted or prohibited AI
services, tell us at kick-off and we will scope the toolchain to it.

## Scope and Fit

### What makes a strong project?

An open-ended business question where the answer is not known in advance, where the decision
recurs so a repeatable framework is worth more than a one-off analysis, and where enough data
exists for the team to work with. See the [RFP](05-rfp.qmd) for detail.

### What makes a weak project?

A task that is already specified and just needs hands, work that requires proprietary systems
access we cannot get, anything safety- or compliance-critical, or a question whose answer you
already know and want validated.

### Can the scope change mid-year?

Yes, in writing. Changes get documented in the decision log and confirmed in the weekly update.
What we manage against is quiet expansion, where questions are added without anything coming off
the plan.

### What if the project isn't going well?

Contact the program director immediately. Most engagement problems are fixable in week 5. Early
intervention is normal program operation, not an escalation.

## Working Arrangements

### How much of my time does this take?

About an hour a week: a 30 to 45 minute standing call, plus reading the weekly update and
answering the decisions it asks for. Plus four milestone reviews across the year.

### Do we need to be local to Utah?

No. Engagements run remote by default. On-site visits are welcome but not required.

### Do we provide equipment or accounts?

Students use their own machines. You may need to provision accounts for data or systems access,
which we will scope at kick-off.

### Can we hire the students?

Yes, and many sponsors do. Recruiting access is one of the real benefits of sponsorship. Please
route offers through the program director during the engagement so it does not disrupt the team.

### Can we extend or run a second project?

Yes. Follow-on engagements and paid summer extensions are both common. Extensions are optional
and not part of the base program.
